title: Palindrome Partitions
statement:
Split a string into consecutive pieces so that every piece reads the same forwards and backwards, and list all such splits.

Contract
- `text` is a non-null string; characters are compared exactly (case-sensitive). It may be empty.
- A partition cuts `text` into consecutive non-empty pieces that, joined in order, give back `text`. Every piece must be a palindrome. A single character is a palindrome.
- Return every valid partition once, each as the list of its pieces in order. The order of the partitions does not matter.
- The empty string has exactly one partition, the one with no pieces, so the result is `[[]]`.

Examples
- `partitions("aab")` returns `[["a", "a", "b"], ["aa", "b"]]` in any order.
- `partitions("abc")` returns `[["a", "b", "c"]]`.
- `partitions("racecar")` returns four partitions, among them `["racecar"]` and `["r", "aceca", "r"]`.
hints: Choose the first piece, then partition what is left. The first piece can end at any position, but only if it is a palindrome.
Recurse on the remainder with the current pieces kept in a list; when the start index reaches the end of the text, copy the list into the results. Undo the last piece before trying the next cut.

Checking each candidate piece from scratch repeats work. Precompute a table of which substrings are palindromes (a substring is one when its end characters match and its inside is one). The probe uses a string with no palindrome longer than one character. Intended complexity: O(n^2) time and O(n^2) space for the table on that family; the number of partitions can be exponential in general.
inputSyntax: Input: the text, for example: aab
